import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Mathoverflow 347178

*Reference:* [mathoverflow/347178](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/347178)
asked by user [*Biagio Ricceri*](https://mathoverflow.net/users/149235/biagio-ricceri)
-/

open Real Set
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Mathoverflow347178

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Is it true that
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x) = \sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$$?

Answer: No. A counterexample in $\mathbb R^2$ is recorded in the linked formal proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 26,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/fc20c0b55eab6fc26e2bb5b24fb3005303a0910b"]
theorem mathoverflow_347178 :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 f),
        (BddAbove (range f) ↔ BddAbove (range (fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)))) ∧
        (⨆ x, (f x : EReal)) = ⨆ x, (f (x + gradient f x) : EReal) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Is the boundedness of
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x)$ and $\sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$ equivalent?

Answer: No. The same counterexample is recorded in the linked formal proof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 26,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/commit/fc20c0b55eab6fc26e2bb5b24fb3005303a0910b"]
theorem mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_iff :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (_ : ContDiff ℝ 1 f),
        BddAbove (range f) ↔ BddAbove (range fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f : \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,  n \geq 2$ be a $C^1$ function. Does the equality
$$\sup_{x \in \mathbb R^n}f(x) = \sup_{x\in \mathbb R^n} f(x+\nabla f(x))$$
hold when both suprema are finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 26]
theorem mathoverflow_347178.variants.bounded_only :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (n ≥ 2) (f : ℝ^n → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
        (h : BddAbove (range f)) (h' : BddAbove (range (fun x ↦ f (x + gradient f x)))),
        (⨆ x, f x) = ⨆ x, f (x + gradient f x) := by
  sorry

end Mathoverflow347178

reformulations.difference: The Lean proposition adds equivalence of boundedness above as a conjunct to the source's equality of suprema, with both suprema taken in EReal.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any real-valued map u, BddAbove (range u) holds exactly when its EReal supremum is not ⊤. Consequently, equality of the two EReal suprema already implies the boundedness equivalence. The additional conjunct does not change the claim. Proved the universally quantified equivalence as Review347178.main_reformulation in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source's answer discusses the variant assuming sup f < ∞. Lean assumes both ranges are bounded above and uses real-valued suprema.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing g(x) = f(x + gradient f x), range g is contained in range f, so boundedness of f automatically supplies the second hypothesis. Both domains are inhabited, hence both ranges are nonempty. For nonempty bounded ranges, coercing the real supremum into EReal gives the EReal supremum, and this coercion is injective. Thus the Lean statement is equivalent to the source's bounded-above variant. Proved as Review347178.bounded_only_reformulation in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: All three declarations are faithful to the source. The MathOverflow answer reports a C¹ counterexample in dimension 2 with sup f = +∞ and sup f(x + ∇f(x)) = 0, supporting both recorded negative answers; it leaves the general bounded-above variant unsettled. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and boundary.lean passed, covering gradient semantics, satisfiable hypotheses, constants, a nonconstant bounded function, and an unbounded coordinate function. The equivalence proofs have no sorryAx dependency. The GitHub formal_proof links were not visited, as prohibited, so their proof provenance was not audited.
